item.title: Survey: Entrepreneurs’ confidence in government hits term low
item.description: Entrepreneurs’ satisfaction with Finland’s government has fallen over the past six months, according to a new survey. The Entrepreneur Gallup, commissioned by the Federation of Finnish Enterprises, shows that 36 per cent of small and medium-sized business owners are satisfied with the government. In May, the figure stood at 42 per cent. Support for the opposition remains lower. Twelve per cent of respondents say they are satisfied with opposition parties.

item.title: Geneva talks end without deal, Zelensky accuses Russia of delay
item.description: Peace talks between Ukraine and Russia ended in Geneva on Wednesday after two days of negotiations marked by disputes over territory and security. The US-mediated discussions closed after a two-hour session on Wednesday, following six hours of talks on Tuesday held in bilateral and trilateral formats. Both sides said they would meet again, though no date was set. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky described the negotiations as “difficult” and accused Moscow of slowing the process.

item.title: Kähärä fall ends Finland medal bid in team sprint
item.description: Finland’s medal bid in the women’s team sprint at the Milan-Cortina Winter Olympics ended in the final descent when Jasmin Kähärä fell metres before the finish line. Kähärä went down in the last bend after the concluding downhill section of the anchor leg. She rose and crossed the line in ninth place. Sweden won gold in 20:29.99, ahead of Switzerland and Germany. Finland finished 43.38 seconds behind. Kähärä told Yle after the race that the fall came as exhaustion took hold

item.title: Orpo and Modi set goal to double Finland-India trade
item.description: Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo met Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Tuesday, with both leaders setting a target to double trade between their countries in the coming years. The meeting formed part of Orpo’s four-day visit to India and took place against the backdrop of a newly concluded EU-India trade agreement. Orpo said the two leaders discussed bilateral ties, the EU’s relationship with India and the war in Ukraine.

item.title: Wille Rydman appointed Finland’s social affairs and health minister
item.description: Finland’s Finns Party has appointed Wille Rydman as the new minister of social affairs and health, replacing Kaisa Juuso, who stepped down last week citing exhaustion and announced she would take sick leave. The party’s parliamentary group and executive board confirmed the decision on Wednesday. Helsingin Sanomat first reported the appointment. Party leader and Finance Minister Riikka Purra said the choice was unanimous.

item.title: Thousands of Asko and Sotka customers face lost orders after bankruptcy
item.description: At least 15,000 customers who paid in advance for furniture from Finnish chains Asko and Sotka are unlikely to receive their orders following the bankruptcy of owner Indoor Group, the court-appointed administrator has said. Administrator Tuomas Penttilä told STT that up to nearly 20,000 customer orders are currently stuck in the bankruptcy estate. “Unfortunately, the lion’s share of these products are such that consumer creditors will not receive them,” he said.

item.title: Finland stun Switzerland to reach Olympic ice hockey semi-finals
item.description: Finland reached the Olympic semi-finals after overturning a two-goal deficit to beat Switzerland 3–2 in overtime in Milan on Tuesday night. For more than 50 minutes, the quarter-final slipped from Finland’s grasp. Switzerland led 2–0 midway through the third period and defended in numbers. Then the momentum turned. Sebastian Aho ignited the comeback at 53:54 with a wrist shot that cut the deficit to 2–1.

item.title: Ex-prince Andrew arrested on misconduct suspicion
item.description: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has been arrested on suspicion of misconduct in public office after police opened an investigation linked to his dealings with the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. Thames Valley Police said officers detained a man in his sixties from Norfolk on Thursday morning and carried out searches at addresses in Berkshire and Norfolk. item.title: Finland take Olympic silver after final sprint duel with Norway
item.description: Finland claimed Olympic silver in the Nordic combined team event after Norway secured gold by 0.5 seconds in a sprint finish. Ilkka Herola and Eero Hirvonen led Finland to the podium in the large hill and 2x7.5km relay at the Milano-Cortina Winter Games. The race remained undecided until the final straight, where Jens Lurås Oftebro edged ahead of Hirvonen in deep snow on the finishing stretch. Norway crossed the line first. item.title: Iran and US expand military readiness amid nuclear negotiations
item.description: Iran has reinforced key military and nuclear facilities with concrete and earth barriers as the United States increases its military presence in the Middle East and President Donald Trump renews threats of action if talks fail. New satellite images published by Reuters and verified by BBC Verify show extensive construction at sensitive Iranian sites, including the Parchin military complex southeast of Tehran.
